title: Exercise 7B · Q12
summary: The longest side (x + 2) must be the hypotenuse — form and solve a quadratic.
alt: Exercise 7B · Q12: A folded napkin has a triangular cross section of sides x cm, (x + 1) cm and (x + 2) cm. If one of the angles of the triangle is 90°, find the value of x.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A folded napkin has a triangular cross section of sides **x cm**, **(x + 1) cm** and **(x + 2) cm**. One angle of the triangle is **90°**. Find the value of **x**.

steps.title: The longest side is the hypotenuse
steps.narration: **(x + 2) cm** is the longest side, so it must be the **hypotenuse**.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{(x+2)^2} &= \role{legA}{x^2} + \role{legB}{(x+1)^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Form a quadratic equation
steps.narration: Bring every term to one side.\[\begin{aligned}x^2 - 2x - 3 &= 0\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Factorise and solve
steps.narration: Factorise, then read off the roots.\[\begin{aligned}(x - 3)(x + 1) &= 0 \\ x = 3 \;&\text{or}\; x = -1\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Choose the valid value
steps.narration: A length can't be negative, so reject **x = −1**.\[\begin{aligned}\therefore x = \role{ans}{3}\quad(\text{since } x > 0)\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

challenges.title: Check x = 3
challenges.prompt: If x = 3, the sides are 3, 4 and 5. What is the longest side (the hypotenuse)?

takeaways: When sides are given as **x, x+1, x+2**, the **longest** expression is always the hypotenuse.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: A famous triple
notes.text: x = 3 gives sides **3, 4, 5** — the smallest and most famous Pythagorean triple.
